Leprosy

The ulcer trial found no additional healing, while one neuropathy trial cohort reported improvement in selected sensory and functional outcomes. Its later report comes from the same participants.

Clinical effect sizes (estimate)

Chronic ulcers — The 2010 trial found no significant differences in ulcer area, depth, or PUSH after 12 weeks; no between-group estimates were reported in the abstract (Barreto and Salgado 2010).

Leprosy-related neuropathy — In the 2025 report of the 30-person cohort, severe SALSA activity limitation decreased (effect size 0.24). Median- and tibial-nerve functional measures improved in the PBM-plus-physiotherapy arm (P=0.0281 and P=0.0267). Pain improved within both arms but did not differ between groups (Bonazza et al. 2025).

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Low certainty for selected nerve-function and activity outcomes with PBM added to physiotherapy. Two papers report the same 30-person Brazilian cohort; they are not independent trials (Duarte et al. 2023; Bonazza et al. 2025).

Very low certainty for chronic ulcer healing: one small randomized trial found no added healing benefit (Barreto and Salgado 2010).

PBM Database summary

What the records report

The ulcer trial found no additional healing, while one neuropathy trial cohort reported improvement in selected sensory and functional outcomes. Its later report comes from the same participants.

Summary of the Evidence

Three publications address two distinct randomized cohorts. One 2010 trial studied chronic ulcers in people with leprosy sequelae. The other cohort enrolled 30 people for a physiotherapy comparison with or without PBM; its 2023 and 2025 articles share the same Brazilian trial-registration identifier and should be treated as two reports from one cohort, not as independent trials. No animal or separate in-vitro study of PBM for leprosy complications was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

In the 2010 ulcer trial, 25 of 51 assessed patients were randomized. The 97 ulcers had a mean duration of 97.6 ± 111.7 months, mean area of 7.3 ± 11.5 cm², and mean depth of 6.0 ± 6.2 mm. After 12 weeks, ulcer area, depth, and PUSH healing scores did not differ significantly between laser and control, so the tested protocol did not demonstrate additional healing benefit (Barreto and Salgado 2010).

The separate neuropathy trial compared physiotherapy alone (PPG) with physiotherapy plus PBM (PPBMG) in 30 participants over four weeks. Its 2023 report described better activity-limitation, pain, nerve-palpation, strength, and sensitivity measures in several domains for the combined group; numerical estimates were not provided in the abstract (Duarte et al. 2023). In the 2025 report from the same cohort, fewer PPBMG participants had severe activity limitation (effect size 0.24), and more had no participation restriction. Median- and tibial-nerve functional measures improved in PPBMG (P=0.0281 and P=0.0267); ulnar-nerve palpation improved in PPG (P=0.0244) and fibular-nerve palpation in PPBMG (P=0.0425). Pain improved within both groups (PPG, P=0.0061; PPBMG, P=0.041), with no between-group difference. Several SF-36 domains improved in both groups (Bonazza et al. 2025). These findings are outcome-specific, and the two articles are reports from one cohort.

Animal evidence

No animal study directly examining PBM for leprosy-related neuropathy or ulcers was identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No separate cell or tissue study directly testing these leprosy outcomes was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The ulcer trial used a TWIN LASER (MM Optics, São Paulo, Brazil), a continuous 660-nm red visible laser at 40 mW. It delivered 4 J per point to wound edges and 2 J/cm² to wound beds, three times weekly for 12 weeks. The neuropathy protocol used pulsed 904-nm near-infrared light at 70 mW for nine seconds per point over 12 sessions in four weeks alongside physiotherapy. The targets differ, and there was no dose-finding comparison (Barreto and Salgado 2010).

Interpretation

One small ulcer trial found no additional healing with the tested red-light protocol. In one separate neuropathy cohort, selected activity and nerve-function measures improved, while the later report found no between-group pain difference. The 2023 and 2025 articles are two reports from that cohort, not independent trials.

Rationale for the certainty assessment

One 30-person cohort reported selected nerve and activity improvements with PBM added to physiotherapy; its 2023 and 2025 reports are linked. Pain improved in both arms without a between-group difference in the later report. One ulcer RCT found no added healing. Independent, adequately powered trials are needed (Duarte et al. 2023; Bonazza et al. 2025; Barreto and Salgado 2010).
